## Exact additive contracts

- `types.ts` exports `NoticeChannel = "action" | "hazard" | "system" | "persistence"`, `NoticeContext = "threat" | "oxygen" | "food" | "hull" | "recovery"`, and `NoticeOptions { channel?: NoticeChannel; context?: NoticeContext }`. The existing notice variant intersects those options and retains `message`/`error`. Command results/refusals are action. Survival notices use hazard/oxygen, hazard/food, hazard/hull and hazard/recovery for actual incapacity recovery. Threat notices use hazard/threat. The existing `updateRecovery` notice is tagged at step composition: action/recovery for progress, hazard/recovery for errors. The error check is confined to that explicitly identified recovery result; no general error/string classifier exists. `recovery.ts` is unchanged.
- `SessionEvents.notify(message: string, error?: boolean, options?: NoticeOptions): void` is backward compatible with existing two-argument callbacks. Existing save/new/import acknowledgements use persistence and explicit `false`; save/import-write failures, session-only and unavailable/recovered Continue reminders use persistence. Cancellation, Continue migration and invalid/oversized/future/unreadable files use system with their original error values. No notification, text, async work, writer/commit/fallback choice or lifecycle ordering was added or changed.
- Sound gains optional `source?: "threat-call"`. Only the existing positional warning calls on actual warn/pursue transitions receive it. Their detached emitted origins, cues and positions in the event sequence remain identical. No repeated call/timer or tracking state exists; body/equipment/damage sounds retain their old fields. A later cue must use the emitted copy rather than continuously reading the animal position.
- `survival.ts` exports `SUIT_OXYGEN_DRAIN_PER_SECOND = 100 / 180` and read-only `airSupply(s: GameState): { kind: "craft" | "refuge" | "surface" | "emergency" | "suit"; remainingSeconds: number | null }`. Its precedence is healthy powered controlled craft, actual exposure refuge, actual airway surface, controlled craft positive emergency reserve, then current suit oxygen divided by that shared drain. Continuous air has null seconds; finite supplies never combine or reset. Existing `exposure` shape/rules are unchanged.
- `GameEvent` gains transient `{ type: "ascent-sample"; actorId: string | null; requestedRise: number; actualRise: number; solidLimitedRise: number; surfaceLimitedRise: number }`, in metres for this fixed step. Actor null means swimmer. At most one is appended after existing events, only for positive commanded upward intent with positive current velocity-derived intended rise. Swim requests sum the existing slice requests before support correction; piloting uses the existing velocity delta. Positive Y loss is measured from actual raw `hitSolid` sweep results before floor corrections, and surface-cap loss separately. `actualRise` keeps the signed final net movement, including negative slides.

Piloted measurement delegates the existing `moveHull` queries through a local observing wrapper: its aggregate `hitSolid` also reports terrain support, so that aggregate cannot classify a ceiling. No query is replayed, and all computations, calls, movement order and values remain unchanged. The sample is omitted for release/down/no upward intent, passive inertia, walking/interior/opening/mode transitions, Spindle, station keeping, disabled/unpowered craft, same-step disable/incapacity or actor replacement. Absence is the later app's reset signal. There is no sim history, WeakMap, saved timer, cache, queue or UI behavior.

The existing actual-refuge predicates exclude a controlled craft at the pod/workshop/lab. Tests retain that distinction: physical overlap alone does not grant refuge air. A healthy craft overlapping lab coordinates reports craft; an unpowered submerged craft there reports its actual finite reserve. A genuinely breathable surface or station-kept interior uses external air. No refuge rule was broadened to satisfy a label.
